# spec

Design requirements for the delulu-smash app (`services/ui`), kept apart from `services/ui/README.md`,
which documents what is built. One file per concern. The spec says what must hold, the README says what
does.

## The spirit of the app

> *The simplicity & efficiency of Omarchy, the exploration of Jupyter, the composability of VS Code, and the
> extensibility & flexibility of Pi: your desktop hub.*

This is the app's mantra (the user's, Nov 2026), and every rule in this spec serves it. Each new feature and
design choice gets checked against all five parts. When one is traded off for another, say so.

| Part | What it means here | Already in the app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Simplicity & efficiency of Omarchy** | Keyboard first, one letter per action, nothing on screen that isn't needed, every list searchable. It looks and behaves like the desktop around it | `Alt` keys, `Alt+K` list, `Alt+P` palette, panels hidden until wanted ([omarchy.md](omarchy.md)) |
| **Exploration of Jupyter** | Every result is a live value you can keep, poke at and build on, in the AI chat or in code. Asking a question and working on the answer are one flow | results as `r1`, `r2`, … ; Python cells; Variables panel; `@name` mentions ([variables.md](variables.md)) |
| **Composability of VS Code** | Pieces combine and rearrange instead of each living in one fixed place: panels are shown, hidden, split and zoomed to fit the task; a widget is the same wherever it is put (a Results tab, the chat, under a cell, floating); one value flows between the chat, the cells and the widgets; every action, whatever adds it, sits in the same palette and keys | panels with `Alt` keys and ⤢ / ×; widgets in tabs, chat, cells, Alt+F floating; `r1` used in cells and `@r1` in the chat; the `Alt+P` palette and slash commands |
| **Extensibility & flexibility of Pi** | As with the Pi coding agent: a small core that grows by adding pieces (widgets, tools, commands) as data, not by editing the core. The user shapes it to their own workflow, and the AI helps build the new pieces | `WIDGETS` rows, the palette / slash commands made from them, inline AI filling any widget's inputs ([inline_ai.md](inline_ai.md)) |
| **Your desktop hub** | One place for Smash work (data, VODs, AI, code), always running as a desktop app and not a site you visit | `SUPER+SHIFT+I`, `delulu-smash.service` |

## Words: panel and widget

Two different things, and the design rules differ for each. Use these words (the user's, Nov 2026); older text
and the code say "pane" for a panel.

| | Panel | Widget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | a fixed region of the window's layout: a place | a view of one value: a thing shown in a place |
| Which | Chat, Results, Python, Variables, Terminal (experiment) | table, VODs, player usage, fields, SmashDb console, Browser |
| How many | one of each; shown or hidden (the bottom bar, `Alt` keys) | any number; the same value can be shown in several places |
| Where defined | the layout in `ui/ui.py` | a row in `WIDGETS` (`ui/widgets.py`), drawn by `render.py` |
| Holds | widgets, cells, messages | its own controls and state (filter, sort, inputs) |

Design rules that follow from the difference:

- **Panels are flush and uniform.** They touch their neighbours with one dividing line, no gap and no frame of
  their own, and the strip at the top of each is the same height (`--panel-head` in `assets/app.css`), so they
  line up when several are open.
- **A widget is self-contained and the same wherever it is placed** (a Results tab, the chat, under a cell):
  it keeps its own frame and brings its controls with it. See the README's "Rendering" design rule.
- A new region of the window is a panel; a new way to show a value is a widget. Don't give a panel a widget's
  frame, or build a widget that only works in one panel.

## Panels: what every panel has

The same controls on every panel, so learning one teaches all of them (Omarchy's "one pattern everywhere").
A new panel gets all of these; a panel missing one is a bug.

| | Rule | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Key** | `Alt+<letter>` shows or hides it, from anywhere, **including from inside it**: a panel whose content takes the keyboard (the Terminal's shell) hands its own keys back to the app. Showing it by its key puts the cursor in it | `Alt+A` chat (AI), `Alt+R` Results, `Alt+J` Python (Jupyter), `Alt+V` Variables, ``Alt+` `` Terminal (VS Code's terminal key, Ctrl+\`, with the app's Alt) |
| **Full screen** | `Alt+Shift+<the same letter>` fills the window with it, from anywhere, even when hidden; the same key again puts the layout back. `Alt+F` does it for the panel you are in | `Alt+Shift+A` / `R` / `J` / `V` / `` ` `` |
| **Title strip** | the same height on every panel (`--panel-head`), flush with its neighbours; it ends with ⤢ (full screen) and × (close: the same as its key). Its title may be left out to keep the panel bare (the chat has none; its model is in the window's title bar) | `zoom_button`, `close_button` in `ui/ui.py` |
| **Bottom bar** | one toggle per panel, lit while it is shown, in panel order | 🤖 ▦ 🐍 ⚙ >_ |
| **Palette** | a "Show / Hide <panel>" row and a "Full screen: <panel>" row in `Alt+P` | `commands.py` |
| **Closing keeps it** | hiding a panel (key, ×, bottom bar) only hides it: what is in it stays (cells, variables, the shell). Only a page reload starts it over | `.is-hidden` (CSS), not unmounted |
| **Takes the space** | a panel whose neighbour is hidden takes the freed space; nothing leaves a gap | `*_layout` in `state.py` (hidden / alone / split) |
| **Defined once** | its keys in `ui/shortcuts.py` (so they show in `Alt+K` and the help), its name in `state.PANES` | |

Choosing a letter: Omarchy's own letter for the same action first (see [omarchy.md](omarchy.md)), else the
first letter that says what it is and is free (`J` for Jupyter because `P` is the palette), or the key
another tool the user knows uses for it (``Alt+` `` for the Terminal, from VS Code's Ctrl+\`).

## The app explains itself

The chat can answer how to use the app (`services/ui/guide.md`, loaded by the chat agent on demand). So:

- **A user-visible feature gets its lines in `guide.md`** in the same change: what to type and what shows,
  no file or function names. Short: the guide is sent whole to the model.
- Lists that exist as data (slash commands, keys) are added from the code, never retyped in the guide.
- The agent answers app questions from the guide only, and says when the guide doesn't cover something.

- [omarchy.md](omarchy.md): navigation, keys and many other parts of the app follow Omarchy, the desktop
  it runs on.
- [inline_ai.md](inline_ai.md): `Alt+I`, the AI that changes what you are in. A widget with a tool is a
  function; the AI fills its inputs and the user runs them.
- [variables.md](variables.md): the Variables pane. Cleared means gone: one short undo, then the memory
  is really released. Also `@name` mentions of variables in the chats (experimental) and `/assign`, a variable whose code the AI writes.
